title: ioctl_do_kdf: out_zero re-locks without a comment explaining why
notes: In ioctl_do_kdf (crypto2dev_fd.c lines 1895-1898), the out_zero label acquires the mutex, calls inbuf_clear, then releases it. All goto-out_zero paths exit BEFORE mutex_lock at line 1776, so the lock is never held when out_zero is reached. The re-acquire is intentional: these are pre-lock validation failures that still need to zeroize any IKM written via write() before the ioctl. The problem: (1) no comment explains WHY out_zero needs its own lock — a reader sees mutex_lock in a cleanup label and must trace every goto path to understand the invariant; (2) a future maintainer consolidating cleanup paths could easily collapse out_zero and out_inbuf_clear, creating a double-lock if reached from a post-lock path, or omitting the zeroize if reached from a pre-lock path. Recommended fix: add a comment at out_zero: '/* Reached only from pre-lock validation paths — lock not held; re-acquire to zeroize any pending IKM written before this ioctl. */' This is the only P1 maintainer-burden finding from SEC1 review.
